title: Stanford Alpaca
creators: Stanford CRFM (Rohan Taori, Ishaan Gulrajani, Tianyi Zhang, Percy Liang, Tatsunori Hashimoto et al.)
description: LLaMA-7B fine-tuned on 52K instructions generated by OpenAI's text-davinci-003, for under $600.
capabilityNote: Established the cheap instruction-tuning-by-distillation recipe behind hundreds of later fine-tunes; the public demo was pulled within days over cost and safety concerns.

majorUpdates.title: Demo pulled
majorUpdates.summary: The web demo was taken down over cost and safety concerns.

title: Vicuna / FastChat
creators: LMSYS Org (Wei-Lin Chiang, Lianmin Zheng, Ying Sheng, Ion Stoica, Joseph Gonzalez et al.)
description: LLaMA-13B fine-tuned on about 70K ShareGPT conversations, released with FastChat, the serving and evaluation stack that later hosted Chatbot Arena and MT-Bench.
capabilityNote: Popularized "GPT-4 as a judge" evaluation; its quality claims rested on that judge rather than on human-graded benchmarks.

majorUpdates.title: MT-Bench / LLM-as-a-judge
majorUpdates.summary: Paper formalizing GPT-4-as-judge evaluation.

majorUpdates.title: Vicuna v1.5
majorUpdates.summary: Rebased on Llama 2.

title: Chatbot Arena (LMArena)
description: A crowdsourced leaderboard where users vote between two anonymous chatbots' answers, ranked with an Elo-style rating.
capabilityNote: Became the most-cited preference leaderboard; it measures which answers people prefer, not correctness, and labs were later criticized for testing private variants on it.

majorUpdates.title: LMArena raises $100M

majorUpdates.title: Raises $150M at $1.7B, rebrands to Arena

title: Mistral / Mixtral
creators: Mistral AI (Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample, Timothée Lacroix)
description: Mistral 7B, released via a magnet link, beat Llama 2 13B; Mixtral 8x7B (Dec 2023) popularized sparse Mixture-of-Experts in open weights.
capabilityNote: Apache licensing made it the default commercial open base in late 2023; some later models used a more restrictive research licence.

title: Qwen (Alibaba)
description: An open-weight family with a broad size ladder (0.5B to 397B MoE) plus Coder, VL and Omni variants; the most-forked open base on Hugging Face by 2025.
capabilityNote: Became the default base for academic RL and reasoning work; the first release date is from the researcher's memory.

majorUpdates.title: Qwen2
majorUpdates.summary: Second generation.

majorUpdates.summary: Widely used coding variants.

majorUpdates.title: Qwen3.6
majorUpdates.summary: Open weights under Apache-2.0 while Qwen3.6-Plus stayed proprietary.

title: DeepSeek-V3 / V4
description: A 671B-parameter MoE model (37B active) with a reported ~$5.6M final training run, released with open weights.
capabilityNote: The reported training cost covered only the final run, but the MIT licence and efficiency reset price expectations across the industry.

majorUpdates.title: Open Source Week
majorUpdates.summary: Released FlashMLA, DeepEP, DeepGEMM and 3FS infrastructure code.

majorUpdates.title: DeepSeek-V4 preview
majorUpdates.summary: V4-Pro 1.6T total / 49B active and V4-Flash 284B / 13B active, 1M context, MIT.

majorUpdates.title: V4-Pro-0813 GA
majorUpdates.summary: General availability of V4-Pro (single secondary source).

title: DeepSeek-R1
description: An open-weights reasoning model trained largely with reinforcement learning (GRPO), released with distilled Qwen and Llama versions under MIT.
capabilityNote: Reported 79.8% on AIME 2024, comparable to OpenAI o1; it made RL-trained reasoning reproducible in the open and triggered an Nvidia stock sell-off.

majorUpdates.title: Nature publication
majorUpdates.summary: The R1 paper appeared in Nature.

title: Gemma (Google DeepMind)
description: Google's family of small open models derived from Gemini research, sized for laptops and phones.
capabilityNote: Gemma 1–3 used custom terms of use; Gemma 4 moved to Apache-2.0. Real usage runs through Hugging Face and Ollama, so repo stars understate it.

majorUpdates.title: Gemma 2
majorUpdates.summary: Second generation.

majorUpdates.summary: Multimodal, 128K context.

majorUpdates.title: Gemma 4
majorUpdates.summary: E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B MoE and 31B dense; 256K context; Apache-2.0.

title: OLMo (Ai2)
creators: Allen Institute for AI (Dirk Groeneveld, Noah Smith, Hanna Hajishirzi et al.)
description: A fully open model family that releases weights plus training data, code, logs and intermediate checkpoints.
capabilityNote: The reference point for "truly open source" AI; OLMo 3-Think 32B was billed as the first fully open 32B thinking model.

majorUpdates.title: OLMo 2
majorUpdates.summary: Second generation, with the Tülu 3 post-training recipe.

majorUpdates.title: OLMo 3
majorUpdates.summary: Base, Instruct, Think and RL-Zero variants at 7B and 32B.

title: gpt-oss (OpenAI)
description: gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, MoE reasoning models and OpenAI's first open weights since GPT-2.
capabilityNote: Brought a US frontier lab back into open weights; the 20b model runs on 16GB devices.

title: Kimi K2 / K3 (Moonshot AI)
description: K2 was a 1T-parameter MoE (32B active) tuned for agentic tool use; K3 is the largest open-weight model released so far.
capabilityNote: K3 (2.8T total / 104B active, ~1.4TB of weights) needs 64+ accelerators, and its licence adds revenue-triggered and attribution clauses, so "open" comes with conditions.

majorUpdates.title: K2 Thinking
majorUpdates.summary: Reasoning variant.

majorUpdates.title: Kimi K3
majorUpdates.summary: 2.8T / 104B-active MoE with 1M context under a bespoke licence.

title: GLM (Zhipu / Z.ai)
description: A Chinese open model family, starting with ChatGLM-6B, that by mid-2026 led open-weight agentic coding rankings.
capabilityNote: GLM-5.2 was a 753B MoE, 1M-context, MIT-licensed model; the GLM-5.3 flagship then moved to a bespoke licence aimed at hyperscalers. The 2023 start date is from the researcher's memory.

majorUpdates.title: GLM-4.5
majorUpdates.summary: MIT-licensed agentic model.

majorUpdates.title: GLM-5
majorUpdates.summary: Framed as moving from vibe coding to agentic engineering.

majorUpdates.title: GLM-5.2
majorUpdates.summary: 753B MoE, 1M context, MIT; topped open-weight rankings.

majorUpdates.title: GLM-5.3
majorUpdates.summary: GLM-5.3-Flash under MIT (Aug 26) and the flagship under a bespoke licence.

sources.title: The New Stack on GLM licensing

title: Muse Glimmer (Meta)
description: A 30B-parameter open-weight model under Apache-2.0, optimized for agents and sized for consumer GPUs, released four months after Meta discontinued the open Llama line.
capabilityNote: A partial return to open weights: Meta's flagship Muse Spark stayed closed, with only a promise to open Muse Spark 1.2 weights.

title: llama.cpp / GGUF
description: Plain C/C++ inference for LLaMA-family models with aggressive integer quantization, running on CPUs, Apple Silicon and consumer GPUs.
capabilityNote: Moved LLaMA from datacenter GPUs to a MacBook within weeks of the leak; its GGUF format became the de facto file format for local models.

majorUpdates.title: GGUF format
majorUpdates.summary: Replaced the older GGML file format.

majorUpdates.title: llama-server and more backends
majorUpdates.summary: OpenAI-compatible server, multimodal support, Vulkan/SYCL/Metal backends (2024–25).

title: vLLM
creators: UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab (Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Ion Stoica et al.)
description: A high-throughput LLM serving engine built on PagedAttention (paged KV cache) and continuous batching.
capabilityNote: Reported up to 24× throughput over Hugging Face Transformers at launch and became the default open serving layer; Hugging Face archived its own TGI server in 2026 and now contributes to vLLM.

majorUpdates.title: SOSP paper
majorUpdates.summary: PagedAttention paper published.

majorUpdates.title: V1 engine rewrite
majorUpdates.summary: Core engine rewritten.

majorUpdates.title: Hugging Face TGI archived
majorUpdates.summary: HF's competing server went read-only after maintenance mode in Dec 2025, with users pointed to vLLM and SGLang.

title: FlashAttention
description: IO-aware exact attention that avoids materializing the full N×N attention matrix in GPU memory.
capabilityNote: Made long context economically feasible and now sits in nearly every major training and inference stack.

majorUpdates.title: FlashAttention-2
majorUpdates.summary: Better parallelism and work partitioning.

majorUpdates.title: FlashAttention-3
majorUpdates.summary: Optimized for NVIDIA Hopper.

title: Unsloth
description: Hand-written Triton kernels for faster, lower-memory LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning and RL, plus a major publisher of quantized GGUF models.
capabilityNote: 4-bit QLoRA of an 8B model fits in about 6GB of VRAM; its download figures are vendor claims.

title: LangChain
description: A framework for chaining LLM calls with prompts, tools and retrieval, open-sourced a month before ChatGPT and at the centre of the 2023 RAG wave.
capabilityNote: "LangChain is dead" became a recurring meme as developers moved to provider SDKs and harnesses, yet the company raised $125M at a $1.25B valuation in Oct 2025.

majorUpdates.title: LangSmith beta
majorUpdates.summary: Closed-source tracing and eval platform; GA in Feb 2024 with a $25M Series A.

majorUpdates.title: LangChain 1.0 and $125M Series B
majorUpdates.summary: create_agent now runs on LangGraph's runtime; valuation $1.25B.

title: LangGraph
description: A low-level orchestration framework and durable runtime for agents built as stateful graphs, with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop steps.
capabilityNote: A framework for building agents rather than an agent itself; it became the runtime underneath LangChain 1.0.

majorUpdates.title: LangGraph Platform GA
majorUpdates.summary: Hosted deployment for LangGraph agents.

majorUpdates.title: LangGraph 1.0
majorUpdates.summary: Stable release alongside LangChain 1.0.

title: LlamaIndex
description: A data framework, launched as GPT Index, for connecting LLMs to private data through indexing and retrieval, later adding agent workflows and document parsing.
capabilityNote: RAG-first counterpart to LangChain; retrieval grounds answers but does not stop models from misreading what they retrieve.

title: CrewAI
description: Role-based multi-agent orchestration in which "crews" of agents with roles and goals collaborate, plus deterministic Flows.
capabilityNote: Independent of LangChain since 2024 and still actively developed in 2026.

title: AutoGen / AG2
creators: Microsoft Research (Chi Wang, Qingyun Wu et al.)
description: A multi-agent conversation framework from Microsoft Research; after the v0.4 rewrite its original creators forked it as AG2.
capabilityNote: AutoGen merged into Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 in April 2026 and pushes stopped; the AG2 fork stayed small (under 5K stars).

majorUpdates.title: AG2 fork
majorUpdates.summary: Original creators forked the project as AG2.

majorUpdates.title: AutoGen v0.4
majorUpdates.summary: Architecture rewrite.

majorUpdates.title: Merged into Microsoft Agent Framework
majorUpdates.summary: AutoGen development moved into MAF 1.0.

title: DSPy
description: "Programming, not prompting": declarative LLM modules whose prompts and weights are optimized automatically against a metric.
capabilityNote: Replaced hand-tuned prompt strings with measurable optimization; results still depend on the quality of the metric and examples.

majorUpdates.title: DSP repository
majorUpdates.summary: Precursor project created before the DSPy paper.

title: Dify
description: A visual builder for LLM apps and agents with RAG, workflows and model management, widely adopted in Asia.
capabilityNote: Its modified Apache licence restricts multi-tenant SaaS use and logo removal, so it is source-available rather than plainly open source.

title: n8n
description: A workflow-automation platform that predates the LLM boom and became a popular low-code builder for AI agents.
capabilityNote: Growth came from wiring LLM steps into ordinary business automations; the company reports 1.7M monthly active builders.

majorUpdates.title: €55M Series B
majorUpdates.summary: Funding round.

majorUpdates.title: $180M Series C at $2.5B
majorUpdates.summary: Funding round.

majorUpdates.title: $5.2B valuation via SAP
majorUpdates.summary: SAP strategic investment and embedding in Joule Studio.

title: Flowise
description: A LangChain.js-based drag-and-drop builder for chatflows and agent flows.
capabilityNote: Acquired by Workday in 2025; the repo was archived on Aug 13, 2026 and reached end of life on Aug 31, 2026.

majorUpdates.title: Acquired by Workday
majorUpdates.summary: Workday bought FlowiseAI.

majorUpdates.title: Repository archived
majorUpdates.summary: npm and Docker packages deprecated; end of life Aug 31, 2026.

title: Browser Use
description: A Python library that lets LLMs drive a real browser through the DOM and screenshots via Playwright.
capabilityNote: Became the default open-source browser-agent layer after Manus reportedly used it; browser agents remain slow and error-prone on unfamiliar sites.

title: AutoGPT (and BabyAGI)
description: A script that chained GPT-4 calls in a self-prompting loop toward a user's goal; it became one of GitHub's fastest-growing repos in April 2023.
capabilityNote: In practice it looped aimlessly and burned API credits; it later pivoted to a low-code "continuous agents" platform, and its stars reflect 2023 hype more than current use.

majorUpdates.title: BabyAGI
majorUpdates.summary: Yohei Nakajima's ~140-line task loop, a contemporaneous teaching demo (22,363 stars on Sep 26, 2026).

majorUpdates.title: Low-code agent platform
majorUpdates.summary: Repositioned as a block-based platform for continuous agents.

title: Aider
description: A terminal pair programmer that edits files in a git repo, auto-commits, and uses a tree-sitter "repo map" for context.
capabilityNote: Pioneered terminal coding agents and the widely cited Aider polyglot leaderboard; no pushes since May 2026 suggests development has slowed.

title: OpenHands (ex-OpenDevin)
creators: All Hands AI (Graham Neubig, Robert Brennan, Xingyao Wang)
description: An open autonomous software-engineering agent platform with a sandboxed shell, browser and editor, started as a community response to Devin.
capabilityNote: Posted strong SWE-bench Verified results; funding details come from a secondary source.

title: Cline (ex-Claude Dev)
description: An autonomous coding agent in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal that plans, edits files and runs commands with per-step approval.
capabilityNote: Spawned forks including Roo Code and Kilo; Anthropic blocked it from Claude subscription OAuth in January 2026.

majorUpdates.title: $32M seed and Series A
majorUpdates.summary: Funding led by Emergence and Pace.

majorUpdates.title: Blocked from Claude subscription OAuth
majorUpdates.summary: Anthropic cut off subscription-based access for third-party harnesses.

title: Roo Code
description: A fork of Cline with custom modes, pitched as "a whole dev team of AI agents" in the editor.
capabilityNote: Reached 3 million installs and was then shut down so the company could focus on Roomote; the repo was archived on May 15, 2026.

majorUpdates.title: Shutdown announced
majorUpdates.summary: The team said it would shut Roo Code down to go all-in on Roomote.

majorUpdates.title: Repository archived
majorUpdates.summary: Users pointed to Zoo Code (community fork), Kilo and Cline.

title: goose (Block)
description: An extensible local agent that works with any LLM and was built on MCP from launch.
capabilityNote: A founding project of the Agentic AI Foundation; its repo and governance moved to the foundation in April 2026.

majorUpdates.title: Moves to AAIF
majorUpdates.summary: Repository and governance transferred to the Agentic AI Foundation.

title: OpenCode
description: A model-agnostic open-source terminal coding harness supporting 75+ providers, including local models through Ollama.
capabilityNote: Reported about 650K monthly active users within five months (other figures claim more); the original Go project of the same name was renamed Crush by Charm.

majorUpdates.title: Claude OAuth block
majorUpdates.summary: Anthropic blocked OpenCode from Claude subscription OAuth; OpenCode gained about 18,000 stars in two weeks.

title: OpenClaw
description: A local-first, always-on personal agent harness that users chat with over WhatsApp, Telegram or Slack, with a ClawHub skills marketplace; it began as Warelay and was renamed Clawdbot, Moltbot and then OpenClaw.
capabilityNote: The most-starred repo created since Sep 2025, and 2026's first major AI security crisis: nine CVEs in four days, about 135K exposed instances and 1,184 malicious skills (≈20% of ClawHub) in March 2026.

majorUpdates.title: Renamed Moltbot
majorUpdates.summary: Clawdbot renamed after Anthropic trademark concerns.

majorUpdates.title: Renamed OpenClaw
majorUpdates.summary: Final rename during the viral January wave.

majorUpdates.summary: Nine CVEs in four days, ~135K exposed instances and 1,184 malicious skills.

majorUpdates.title: OpenClaw 2.0 (v2026.8.1)
majorUpdates.summary: Rebuilt Control UI, SQLite sessions, permission modes and private credential prompts; 16,977 PRs from 987 contributors.

title: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
description: A self-hosted, model-agnostic personal agent with a learning loop that writes and refines its own skills, persistent memory, scheduling, subagents and chat front ends, plus a command to import OpenClaw setups.
capabilityNote: The main OpenClaw challenger; Nous was reported in talks to raise at least $75M at a $1.5B valuation. Its launch date differs across sources (Feb 25 per Nous; v0.2.0 on Mar 12 per a third party).

majorUpdates.title: v0.2–v0.6
majorUpdates.summary: Profiles, MCP server mode and Docker support.

majorUpdates.title: Hermes Desktop preview
majorUpdates.summary: Native cross-platform GUI (MIT).

majorUpdates.title: $1.5B funding talks
majorUpdates.summary: Reported talks to raise at least $75M.

majorUpdates.title: v0.21.0 "The Pantheon Release"
majorUpdates.summary: Voice and bot-to-bot messaging across machines.

title: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
description: A Node.js agent runtime in developer preview built around the idea that "everything is a plugin".
capabilityNote: Reported the fastest star growth on record (~112K in ~53 hours); too new to judge sustained use, and star velocity should be read against research on fake GitHub stars.

title: Stable Diffusion
creators: CompVis (Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Patrick Esser, Björn Ommer)
description: A latent diffusion text-to-image model, trained on LAION-5B, small enough to run on consumer GPUs and released with open weights.
capabilityNote: Moved image generation from closed APIs to anyone's PC and enabled LoRAs, ControlNet and Civitai; lawsuits such as Getty v. Stability and CSAM found in LAION are the reality check.

majorUpdates.title: SD 2.0
majorUpdates.summary: Second generation.

majorUpdates.title: SDXL 1.0
majorUpdates.summary: Larger base model.

majorUpdates.title: SD3 Medium
majorUpdates.summary: Licence and anatomy backlash.

majorUpdates.title: SD 3.5
majorUpdates.summary: Latest major release; key researchers left Stability in 2024 to found Black Forest Labs.

title: ComfyUI
description: A node-graph GUI, API and backend for diffusion pipelines covering image, video, audio and 3D.
capabilityNote: Displaced AUTOMATIC1111's web UI (which still has more stars but stalled after mid-2024) as the workflow standard; user and node counts are company claims.

majorUpdates.title: Comfy Org founded
majorUpdates.summary: Company formed; $16.2M seed across Q4 2024 and May 2025.

majorUpdates.title: $30M at $500M valuation
majorUpdates.summary: Craft Ventures-led round.

title: FLUX (Black Forest Labs)
creators: Black Forest Labs (Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Patrick Esser et al.)
description: A 12B rectified-flow transformer image model from the former Stable Diffusion team that displaced SDXL as the open-weights quality leader.
capabilityNote: Only the smallest variants are Apache-2.0; the [dev] models are non-commercial, so "open" mostly means downloadable.

majorUpdates.title: FLUX.1 Tools
majorUpdates.summary: Editing and control tools.

majorUpdates.title: FLUX.2
majorUpdates.summary: 32B flow-matching transformer with up to 4MP generation and multi-reference editing.

majorUpdates.title: FLUX.2 [klein]
majorUpdates.summary: Generates or edits in under 0.5s; 4B version under Apache-2.0.

title: Whisper (OpenAI)
creators: OpenAI (Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim et al.)
description: An encoder-decoder speech recognition model trained on 680K hours of weakly supervised multilingual audio, released with open code and weights.
capabilityNote: Made near-human transcription free and local, but it is known to hallucinate text during silences, which matters in medical transcription.

majorUpdates.title: large-v2
majorUpdates.summary: Improved large model.

majorUpdates.title: large-v3
majorUpdates.summary: Third large model.

majorUpdates.title: large-v3-turbo
majorUpdates.summary: Faster pruned decoder.

title: NVIDIA NOOA (Object-Oriented Agents)
description: A model-agnostic Python framework where an agent is a Python object: methods are its actions, fields its state, docstrings its prompts and type annotations its contracts. Methods left as '...' are filled in by an LLM at runtime; the rest stay ordinary, deterministic Python.
capabilityNote: Research software from NVIDIA labs, not a product. The paper reports results on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0 and ARC-AGI-3, and the docs warn that generated code needs sandboxing.

sources.title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents (arXiv, Jul 2026)

title: Letta (formerly MemGPT)
creators: Letta (Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders et al.)
description: The MemGPT research project became Letta, a framework and company for stateful agents that manage their own long-term memory.
capabilityNote: 'MemGPT' now names the original memory-management design from the paper; Letta is the framework built on it. Active development has since moved to a new codebase.

sources.title: MemGPT is now part of Letta (Sep 2024)

title: OpenAI Swarm
description: An experimental, educational library from OpenAI for lightweight multi-agent handoffs.
capabilityNote: Explicitly not for production. OpenAI replaced it five months later with the Agents SDK and tells users to migrate; it drew attention far beyond its intended use.

sources.title: openai/swarm README: replaced by the OpenAI Agents SDK

title: Pydantic AI
description: A type-safe Python agent framework from the team behind Pydantic: agents are defined with typed tools, dependencies and structured outputs across model providers.
capabilityNote: Brings ordinary Python typing and validation to agent code rather than a new abstraction; popular with teams already using Pydantic and FastAPI.

title: smolagents (Hugging Face)
creators: Hugging Face (Aymeric Roucher, merve, Thomas Wolf)
description: A deliberately small agent library whose main agent writes its actions as Python code instead of JSON tool calls.
capabilityNote: Code-as-action lets an agent loop, branch and combine tools in one step; it runs generated code, so it needs a sandbox for anything real.

title: Agno (formerly phidata)
description: Phidata relaunched as Agno: a Python framework and runtime for building multimodal agents, running them as services and managing them from a web UI.
capabilityNote: Pitched on speed and simplicity. Its star count is among the highest of any agent framework, but that total includes the phidata years.

sources.title: Introducing Agno: Phidata is now Agno (Jan 2025)

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: OpenAI's open-source framework for multi-agent workflows: agents, handoffs between them, guardrails and built-in tracing. Works with other providers' models too.
capabilityNote: The production successor to Swarm. It launched in Python, with a JavaScript/TypeScript version later in 2025.

sources.title: OpenAI: New tools for building agents (Mar 11 2025)

title: OpenAI Responses API
description: OpenAI's API for building agents: one call that combines chat with built-in tools such as web search, file search and computer use.
capabilityNote: Replaces the Assistants API, which OpenAI is winding down. It is an API, not a framework: the Agents SDK sits on top of it.

sources.title: OpenAI: New tools for building agents (Mar 11 2025)

title: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
description: Google's open-source framework for building agents and multi-agent systems, the same one behind agents in its Agentspace and Customer Engagement Suite.
capabilityNote: Model-agnostic in principle, but most at home with Gemini and Google Cloud deployment.

sources.title: Google Developers Blog: Agent Development Kit (Apr 9 2025)

title: Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
description: An open protocol for AI agents built by different vendors to discover each other and hand work back and forth. MCP connects an agent to tools; A2A connects agents to agents.
capabilityNote: Real signals: stars and official SDKs in five languages. The '150+ organisations' figure counts declared supporters, not production deployments.

majorUpdates.title: Moves to the Linux Foundation
majorUpdates.summary: Vendor-neutral governance; founding members include AWS, Cisco, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow.

majorUpdates.title: 150+ supporting organisations
majorUpdates.summary: SDKs in Python, JavaScript, Java, Go and .NET.

sources.title: Linux Foundation launches the A2A project (Jun 23 2025)

title: AWS Strands Agents
description: AWS's open-source agents SDK built on a model-driven approach: give the model a prompt and tools and let it plan, rather than hand-coding the workflow.
capabilityNote: Used inside AWS before release; runs with Bedrock and other providers. Smaller community than the OpenAI and Google SDKs.

title: Vercel AI SDK
description: A TypeScript toolkit for building AI features and agents in web apps, with one interface across model providers and streaming UI helpers.
capabilityNote: Started as a streaming-chat helper; AI SDK 5 (Jul 2025) added agent-loop controls and an Agent class, which Vercel notes adds convenience rather than new capability.

majorUpdates.title: AI SDK 5: agent loop control
majorUpdates.summary: stopWhen and prepareStep for agent loops, plus an Agent class.

title: Claude Agent SDK
description: The harness that runs Claude Code, opened up for building other agents. Renamed from the Claude Code SDK to reflect uses beyond coding.
capabilityNote: Its core idea is to give the agent a computer (files, a shell, tools) so it works the way a person would, rather than wiring up a workflow by hand.

sources.title: Anthropic: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK (Sep 29 2025)

title: Microsoft Agent Framework
description: Microsoft's open-source SDK for .NET and Python that merges Semantic Kernel's enterprise plumbing with AutoGen's multi-agent orchestration.
capabilityNote: Replaces both; AutoGen went into maintenance when the preview shipped, and Microsoft provides migration tools from each.

majorUpdates.title: Version 1.0
majorUpdates.summary: Stable APIs and long-term support.

title: Agentic AI Foundation formed
description: A Linux Foundation home for open agent standards, launched with MCP (from Anthropic), goose (from Block) and AGENTS.md (from OpenAI) as founding projects.
capabilityNote: Governance, not technology: it moves key agent plumbing out of any single company's control. Members include AWS, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI.

sources.title: Linux Foundation announces the Agentic AI Foundation (Dec 9 2025)
MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation

title: Mastra 1.0
description: A TypeScript-native framework for agents and workflows, from the team that built Gatsby. Public since early 2025; 1.0 marked stable APIs.
capabilityNote: The leading TypeScript option, with real usage (300k+ weekly npm downloads at 1.0, self-reported).
